subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should the Browser plugin reject explicit Chrome MCP `cdpUrl` profiles whenever an operator policy requires a pinned socket, or should maintainers define a supported pinned Chrome MCP transport instead?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes an existing profile path because Chrome MCP cannot carry the custom DNS lookup; choosing whether that fail-closed behavior is the permanent product contract requires maintainer ownership.

options.title: Accept the narrow fail-closed boundary
options.body: Keep the rejection only for explicit restrictive CDP policies, document the migration to the `openclaw` driver, and require live proof before merge.

options.title: Design a Chrome MCP pinning seam
options.body: Pause this branch while maintainers define a supported way for Chrome MCP subprocess attachment to preserve the validated endpoint.

options.title: Retain existing Chrome MCP behavior
options.body: Avoid rejecting current explicit `cdpUrl` profiles and limit this PR to OpenClaw-driver paths until a separate compatibility design is accepted.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the rejection only for explicit restrictive CDP policies, document the migration to the `openclaw` driver, and require live proof before merge.
